rv.q: The feeling and insight offered in this show reward you for braving the discomfort zone.

The show is more inspiriting than innovative, but it’s enough that unlike during the real pandemic, the Bengsons can now invite us into their home, and we wade the rivulets of their loss, side by side.
But what there isn’t is room for questions, and I left My Joy Is Heavy with plenty.
I left with a spring in my step and a song in my heart, a fine parting gift from any new musical.
My Joy Is Heavy is the sort of collective, funereal experience that the ritual of theatre is fundamentally supposed to be.
The ritual magic the couple creates onstage transcends all the woo-woo to become one of my favorite evenings of theater this year.
It’s a beautiful journey in which the audience feels held and seen.
A big-hearted look at one creative couple’s bumpy experiences with life in all its messiness.
Their new show, which opened this week at the Theatre Workshop in the East Village, is yet another successful notch in their belt.

cn.t: Critics find this intimate autobiographical musical about miscarriage and pandemic struggles mostly affecting, praising The Bengsons' vulnerable storytelling and emotional depth, though some question the confessional approach.

vr.q: Overall, this feels like a cross between a warm hug and a catharsis, with every emotional beat earned.
